newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo Republic conflict sparks new refugee exodus.
newsitem.headline: Congo Republic conflict sparks new refugee exodus.

text.p: Intense mortar fire was heard in the Congolese capital Brazzaville early on Friday as a new wave of refugees flooded into Kinshasa to escape the fighting, immigration officials said.

The officials at Kinshasa's main passenger landing point, Beach Ngobila, said almost 2,000 refugees crossed over the river Congo into the Democratic Republic of the Congo (formerly Zaire) on Thursday, and more were streaming in at a similar pace on Friday.
Some were clutching rolled-up mattresses and oil lamps.

The conflict between President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso started two-and-a-half months ago when troops loyal to Lissouba surrounded Sassou's residence as part of a crackdown on private militia.

Talks aimed at finding a peaceful solution to the conflict in Congo Republic are set to resume on Friday in the Gabonese capital Libreville, diplomats said. The talks have been going on for over a month.
Fighting flared up in Brazzaville a week ago after three weeks of relative calm, and renewed shelling was heard in the early hours of Friday, the 37th anniversary of Congo's independence from France.
Refugees are deserting the districts of Talangai, Ouenze, Mfilou and Poto-Poto which, they say, are the targets of systematic shelling.

"There's no way you can stay there, you have to get out -- shells are falling on people's houses," said one refugee, who gave her name as Huguette. She had fled Ouenze in the northern part of the city with her children on Tuesday.
Some refugees are being transferred by bus to a camp at Kinkole, close to Kinshasa's N'Djili airport, near a base of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).

Other refugees are staying with their families, while some want to make their way up river to villages in the north of Congo Republic, despite reports that fighting had broken out this week in the town of Impfondo, 900-km (560 miles) north of Brazzaville.
Immigration officials said negotiations were underway with the UNHCR about financing the boat trip north.
Refugees are also fleeing south-west by road to Pointe Noire and the coast, even though the rainy season has started.

"It's a scene of total desolation," said Aime Bouekassa of the World Health Organisation, a doctor travelling on the road just outside Brazzaville. "A lot of the refugees are women fleeing with children and they're here in the open air with the rains starting again."
